chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is not permissible for a man to marry two sisters (or close aunts) simultaneously, specifically between a woman and her paternal aunt, nor between a woman and her maternal aunt.
ai.seo_question: Can a man marry his aunt and his cousin simultaneously in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar establishes the prohibition of 'Jam' al-Ukhtayn' (simultaneous marriage) specifically extending the rule to include both the paternal aunt (ammah) and maternal aunt (khalah). In Shia jurisprudence, this is derived from the Quranic verse 4:23 and is understood as a permanent prohibition (haram mu'abbad) due to the close kinship ties, distinguishing it from temporary marriage rules. The narration highlights the precision of the Imams in defining the boundaries of marital eligibility to preserve family structure.
